basis: Developmental disability defines the syndrome; cardiac septal defects and strabismus/ptosis have supplied frequencies of 30-79%, despite the definition calling heart defects less common.
Intellectual disability, seizures and callosal abnormalities occur in 80-99%; other variable congenital anomalies lack evidence of common damaging involvement.
Neurodegeneration, skin atrophy and deafness define disease; cataract/retinal dystrophy occur in 30-79%. Skeletal abnormalities at 30-79% omitted at cap; dental caries only 5-29%.
Genetically associated inflammatory bowel disease directly affects intestinal tissue through immune-mediated inflammation.
Hypertrichosis and limb shortening define cutaneous/skeletal involvement; aphasia/mutism are reported at 30-79%, supporting neurologic dysfunction, although ID/delay are only 5-29%.
ABCC8-related permanent neonatal diabetes; motor/social developmental delay and athetosis occur in 1/1 annotated patients, supporting neurologic involvement with limited evidence.
Cellular leiomyoma is predominantly a uterine smooth-muscle tumour, outside these axes; no alternative organ of origin is specified.
Distal congenital joint contractures and intellectual disability are defining manifestations.
Inherited red-cell membrane disorder causing severe hemolytic anemia; no additional common directly damaged organ is established.
Malignancy originates in the female urethra, which belongs to the urinary axis.
Inherited nanophthalmia is a developmental disorder of the eye.
Defined by generalized papular and sclerodermoid skin infiltration; common damaging extracutaneous involvement is not established for this subtype.
Autoimmune neuromuscular-junction disease confined to extraocular and eyelid function, causing ophthalmoplegia, diplopia and ptosis.
Skeletal dysplasia and glycosylation disorder; myopia 20/20 and atrial septal defect 5/5. Cleft palate 10/15 and skin/hair abnormalities 40-67% omitted at cap.
Sensorineural deafness and skin/hair pigmentation abnormalities define WS2; iris heterochromia alone does not impair ocular function.
Disorder of lymph-node lymphoid tissue; this umbrella does not establish a specific infectious, autoimmune or lymphoma mechanism.
Usher type 1 combines congenital sensorineural deafness and vestibular dysfunction with progressive retinal degeneration.
Amyloid deposition damages cerebral vessels, causing defining recurrent intracerebral hemorrhage and cognitive decline.
Osteopetrosis with renal failure, anemia and impaired vision each in 1/1 annotated patients; endocrine/electrolyte findings omitted at cap. Single-patient evidence limits certainty.
Neurologic movement disorder defined by persistent action tremor; skeletal muscles express the movement without primary muscle disease.
Benign tumour arising in vaginal reproductive tissue, outside all 13 axes.
Umbrella for inherited endocrine disorders affecting growth; other organ involvement varies by subtype and is not shared across the group.
Skeletal dysplasia with enlarged epiphyses and severe short stature; lens subluxation and cleft palate lack frequencies establishing involvement in at least 30%.
Skeletal dysplasia and sensorineural deafness define OSMED; cleft palate occurs in 30-79%. Functional eye abnormalities are very rare, at 1-4%.
Brain, heart and eye malformations define trisomy 13; cleft palate occurs in 80-99%. Skeletal anomalies and renal/hearing defects also qualify but are omitted at cap.
